items.item_text: Experience working within a complex health system environment.

Home health and hospice experience with knowledge of standards and regulations, medical procedures, medical terminology, disease categories, and services provided in an ambulatory and institutional setting.
Knowledge of all payer systems, procedures, and regulations including Medicare, Medi-Cal, managed care, and third party and experience obtaining authorizations.

The Non-Clinical Patient Navigator 3 (Patient Navigator) for the UC Davis Health Home Care Services Department requires an in-depth understanding of all programs offered by Home Care Services (HCS) and the broad range of services provided. The Patient Navigator will provide non-clinical support, guidance, and assistance for patients, families, and other healthcare partners as they navigate through the complex healthcare needs of patients throughout the transition to home care. The Patient Navigator is responsible for ensuring patient flow; throughput is a priority by processing all referrals in a timely manner. This position may include intake/referral processing and phone coverage on weekends and/or holidays as needed.
10% - Communication and Collaboration
5% - Insurance Verification/Authorizations
5% - Education and Professional Development
Works effectively in an area with constant interruptions and traffic, including noise from telephones, staff conversations, and office equipment.

Thorough knowledge of computer systems and the ability to effectively utilize software applications including demonstrated proficiency in MS Office Suite and mainframe applications such as web-based search engines.
Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
Ability to exercise initiative and judgment in applying established workflows.
Ability to multitask and set priorities, organize work independently, set-up and maintain manual tracking systems for authorizations, follow-up, etc.
Ability to recognize and maintain confidentiality of patient information and comply with all HIPAA laws.

Ability to identify own professional strengths and weaknesses and to engage in activities designed to enhance effectiveness. Strong customer service, communication, and interpersonal-relationship skills to establish and maintain effective relationships with patients, families, team members, and hospital staff in a wide variety of positions and departments.

Ability to be sensitive and effective with persons representing a broad spectrum of social, ethnic, and economic backgrounds. Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English language and to utilize medical interpretation services.
Strong organizational skills, ability to independently coordinate a variety of tasks and functions, and ability to set priorities and recognize situations requiring clinical intervention.
Ability to be flexible and responsive.
Knowledge and understanding of institutional goals and principles.
Must have the ability to learn the dynamics of a complex organization.
Ability to maintain accurate, up-to-date records/logs, and compose reports, correspondence, and summaries in a comprehensive, organized manner.
Ability to receive and manage customer concerns and complaints in an effective way.
